findings.claim: useAllAlertRuleAbilities (the v1 list, RuleDetails, and useAlertRuleAbility/useAlertRuleAbilities) now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities. That function hard-codes isFederated = false (with a TODO), so federated Mimir groups (source_tenants) are no longer blocked from Update, Delete, Pause and Restore. The v1 list shows Edit for them again.
findings.evidence: Base computed isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group). The new code sets isFederated = false at :243-245. The Edit button at components/rules/RuleActionsButtons.tsx:57 is gated by useAlertRuleAbility(rule, Update). This conflicts with RulesGroup.tsx:69 and RuleDetailsButtons.tsx:38, which still treat federated groups as read-only. RulesTable.test mocks the ability hooks, so no test covers this. Proposed red test (superpowers, not run): an unmocked v1 RulesTable test with a cloud rule whose group.source_tenants=['t1'] and AlertingRuleExternalWrite granted; expect no Edit button.
findings.reason: Accepted by all four seats. All four reasoned it from source and none ran it. Before fixing, make it red with the federated-group RulesTable test described in the evidence.

findings.claim: The 'grafana' case renders <GrafanaRuleListItem> inside rules.map(...) without key={key}.
findings.evidence: The removed <GrafanaRuleLoader key={key}> had the key, and the sibling cases at :165 and :169 still pass it. Without it React logs a missing-key console.error, and per-row state (open menu, modals, silence drawer) can attach to the wrong rule when the filtered list changes. public/test/setupTests.ts:16-21 turns on jest-fail-on-console under CI. react/jsx-key is not in eslint.config.js, so lint will not catch it. Current FilterView.test.tsx seeds only Mimir/Prometheus rules (mattpocock), so no existing test covers this path. Breaches frontend.md (Airbnb: always key iterators). Proposed command (not run): CI=true yarn jest public/app/features/alerting/unified/rule-list/FilterView.test.tsx, after adding a test that renders more than one Grafana rule.
findings.reason: Accepted, reasoned only. Red test first: add a FilterView test that seeds two or more Grafana rules and run it with CI=true so the key warning fails the test.

findings.claim: The view link in the new GrafanaRuleListItem drops { returnTo }. Opening a Grafana rule from the list and coming back loses the user's filters and place.
findings.evidence: The deleted GrafanaRuleLoader.tsx (patch line 1222) built the link with createRelativeUrl(..., { returnTo }). DataSourceRuleListItem.tsx:36-42 still passes it, so the two list item types now behave differently. Proposed red test (superpowers): in GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx, assert the rule link href contains returnTo=.
findings.reason: Accepted. Seats disagreed on severity (open-code-review Minor, superpowers Important). Normalised to Important because it is an observable behavioural regression and inconsistent with the sibling list item. Red test first: the returnTo href assertion.

findings.claim: useAllAlertRuleAbilities now calls groupIdentifier.fromCombinedRule, which calls getDatasourceAPIUid. That throws 'Datasource "<name>" not found' during render when the rule's data source is not registered. The old getRulesSourceName path never threw.
findings.evidence: utils/datasource.ts:299-307 throws. RuleDetails.test.tsx:36,87 had to switch its fixture to rulesSource: mimirDs to avoid exactly this throw. Superpowers rates the production risk low, since v1 CombinedRules come from configured data sources.
findings.reason: Accepted as Minor, reasoned only. The RuleDetails.test fixture change is a workaround, not a fix. A repro is to render with a CombinedRule whose rulesSource name is unregistered.

findings.claim: In the new list view, 'Silence notifications' is shown but clicking it does nothing. The silence drawer only renders when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true, and rule is undefined because GrafanaRuleListItem passes only promRule.

SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer reads only rulerRule.grafana_alert.uid (lines 21 and 44), so the prom rule's uid would be enough. GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx asserts the item exists but never clicks it. findings.reason: ponytail: appendix (2 seats), so not fixed this loop. Unverified: the red test that would settle it is clicking Silence in GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx and expecting the dialog.

findings.claim: Duplicate is wrongly enabled for non-Grafana rules. For a non-Grafana rule, AlertRuleMenu passes skipToken. useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities(undefined) then reports loading=false, so MaybeSupported becomes AlwaysSupported and Duplicate becomes [true, hasPermission(AlertingRuleCreate)], which is ORed into canDuplicate.
findings.evidence: Any user with Grafana alert.rules:create sees Duplicate on Mimir, Loki and Prometheus rules. That includes data sources without a ruler (the base hid these via isRulerAvailable=false) and users without AlertingRuleExternalWrite. It also re-enables Duplicate for plugin-provided Grafana rules when promRule is absent. It reaches the v1 list (components/rules/RuleActionsButtons.tsx:110), the rule viewer and the v2 DataSourceRuleLoader. RulesTable.test hides it by mocking useGrafanaPromRuleAbilities to [false,false]. Proposed red test (superpowers): AlertRuleMenu for a cloud rule without ruler config, grant AlertingRuleCreate, expect no Duplicate menu item.
findings.reason: ponytail: appendix (2 seats), so not fixed this loop. Unverified. Settle it with the AlertRuleMenu cloud-rule Duplicate test. The suggested fix is to return NotSupported when rule is undefined.

findings.claim: The prom ability path gates ModifyExport, Pause, Restore and DeletePermanently on prometheusRuleType.grafana.alertingRule. The ruler path it replaces gated on all Grafana rules, including recording rules. So Grafana recording rules lose Export (and the others) in the new list.
findings.evidence: The base used isGrafanaManagedAlertRule / rulerRuleType.grafana.rule, which includes recording rules. The suggested fix is prometheusRuleType.grafana.rule(rule), keeping the alerting-only check for Silence.
findings.reason: ponytail: appendix (2 seats), so not fixed this loop. Reasoned only.
